details: The European Central Bank (ECB) on July 23, 2026, decided to keep its three key interest rates unchanged, with the deposit facility rate remaining at 2.25%. This move was largely anticipated by the market. However, ECB President Christine Lagarde's statements signaled a "hawkish hold," indicating persistent vigilance against inflation, which remains elevated at 2.8% in the Eurozone, exceeding the 2% target. Lagarde highlighted concerns over volatile energy prices, exacerbated by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, and confirmed the ECB's data-dependent approach, keeping the option open for further rate hikes, potentially as early as September.
title: ECB Maintains Key Rates, Hints at Future Hikes Over Inflation Risks

details: Bitcoin experienced a decline on July 23, 2026, mirroring a broader pullback in the financial markets. This downturn was largely influenced by prevailing macroeconomic headwinds, including a significant rise in oil prices and an increase in Treasury yields, both of which fueled renewed inflation concerns. Adding to the negative sentiment for cryptocurrencies was a perceived decrease in the likelihood of the "Clarity Act" legislation passing in the U.S., which aims to establish a clear regulatory framework for digital assets.
title: Bitcoin Falls Amid Rising Oil Prices, Treasury Yields & US Regulatory Uncertainty
